units: <cite ref="Shabbat 31a:6">Sabb. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>כשאני עומד על ר׳ אחת</he> within the time that I can stand on one leg.
Ḥull. II, 6, v. פִּרְכֵּס II; a. v. fr.—Esp. (sub. נזק) the damage done by an animal’s foot, treading, stamping.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 2b:15">B. Kam. 2ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="U01556"><he>שֵׁן</he></cite>.
Ib. 3ᵃ; a. fr.—תורת (ה)ר׳ the law for the protection of travellers, permission to trade. Tanḥ.
B’shall. 12 (the Sodomites said) בואו ונשכח ת׳ הר׳ וכ׳ come, let us make the law of free trade forgotten in our land; Snh. 109ᵃ; a. e.—לר׳ (v. next w.) in the wake of, for the sake of (cmp. שְׁבִיל).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 97">Gen. R. s. 97</cite> (ref. to <he>רגלי</he>, <cite ref="Numbers 11:21">Num. XI, 21</cite>) <he>כולן לרַגְלִי עלו</he> they all came up (from Egypt) for my sake.
Yalk. Sam. 143 יצחק … לרַגְלוֹ Isaac went down to Gerar, and blessing came down for his sake, a. e.—Du. רַגְלַיִם; pl. רְגָלִים.
<cite ref="Niddah 31a:29">Nidd. 31ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="E00392"><he>הִילּוּךְ</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 10b:28">Ber. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>המתפלל … את רַגְלָיו</he> he that says the prayers (<cite ref="V00831"><he>תְּפִלָּה</he></cite>) must direct his feet (stand straight).
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 3:7">Ḥull. III, 7</cite>, v. <cite ref="S02114"><he>קַרְסוּל</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 4:6">Ib. IV, 6</cite> <he>בהמה … רַגְלֶיהָ</he> an animal that had its hindlegs cut off.

Ber. 32ᵃ כסא של שלש ר׳ a chair with three legs (the merits of the three patriarchs); a. v. fr.—מאין הר׳, v. אַיִן II.—מי ר׳, v. מַיִם.—ר׳ לדבר (the thing has feet to stand on,) there is a basis, a reason for it.
<cite ref="Mishnah Nazir 9:3">Naz. IX, 3</cite> <he>שר׳ לד׳</he> for there is a reason (to assume that the field once was a burial ground).
<cite ref="Mishnah Nazir 9:4">Ib. 4</cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: [pilgrimage,] one of the three festivals (Ex. XXIII, 14).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Moed Katan 3:5">M. Kat. III, 5</cite> <he>שלשה … קודם לר׳</he> three days before a festival.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 19a:9">Ib. 19ᵃ</cite>, sq. <he>ערב הר׳</he> the eve of a festival.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 20a:1">Ib. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>כל שהוא משום אבל הר׳ מפסיקו וכ׳</he> an intervening festival interrupts whatever concerns the mourning itself (and the mourning observances must be continued after the festival).
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 19:32">Num. R. s. 19</cite> <he>ועשו את הר׳ וכ׳</he> they observed the festival in Tishri, and after the festive season they took up the war against Sihon.
<cite ref="Yoma 21a:1-3">Yoma 21ᵃ</cite> <he>בשעה … עולין לר׳</he> when the Israelites went to the Temple for the festive visit.

<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 4b:2">R. Hash. 4ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>שמיני ר׳ בפני וכ׳</he> the eighth day of Succoth is an independent festival; a. v. fr.—<he>ר׳ רדופין</he>, v. <cite ref="T00266"><he>רָדַף</he></cite>.—Pl. as ab.

<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 1:1">R. Hash. I, 1</cite> the first of Nisan is <he>ראש השנה … ולר׳</he> is the beginning of the year for the date of the years of kings and for the order of the festivals (making Passover the first).
<cite ref="Pesachim 8b:4">Pes. 8ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>עולי ר׳</he> pilgrims to the Temple, v. supra.
<cite ref="Eruvin 40b:9">Erub. 40ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>שלשה ר׳</he> the three festivals.
Ib. לא איקרו ר׳ they (New Year and Day of Atonement) are not called r’galim (pilgrims’ festivals); a. fr.
